title: Russia claims recapture of Sudzha as Ukrainian position in Kursk Oblast collapses
body:
On 13 March 2025, the Russian Defense Ministry said its forces had retaken Sudzha, a town in Kursk Oblast that Ukrainian troops had captured at the start of their incursion into Russia in August 2024. The Kyiv Independent reported that it could not immediately verify the claim. The ministry also said Russian forces had taken the settlements of Melovoi and Podol and published unverified video of the ruined town.

Sudzha had a pre-war population of about 6,000 and lies roughly 10 kilometres from the border. On 12 March, Valery Gerasimov, chief of the Russian General Staff, said Russia had retaken more than 86 percent of the Kursk Oblast territory that Kyiv had captured in mid-2024.

DeepState and the Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian forces had partially or fully seized Sudzha and that Ukraine was allegedly withdrawing. Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi acknowledged a "difficult situation" but said Ukraine would hold its defenses "as long as reasonable and necessary." Andrii Kovalenko, an official at the National Security and Defense Council, said Russian airstrikes had almost entirely destroyed the town.

Kyiv had sought to use its positions in Kursk Oblast as leverage in potential negotiations. According to the Kyiv Independent, it began losing ground in the region around the time the United States temporarily paused military and intelligence support for Ukraine.
